# cxpy

> Add elements of a one-dimensional single-precision complex floating-point ndarray to the corresponding elements of a second one-dimensional single-precision complex floating-point ndarray and assign the results to the second ndarray.

<section class="intro">

This BLAS extension implements the operation

<!-- <equation class="equation" label="eq:xpy" align="center" raw="\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{x} + \mathbf{y}" alt="Equation for xpy operation."> -->

```math
\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{x} + \mathbf{y}
```

<!-- </equation> -->

This API is a specialized version of the package [`@stdlib/blas/ext/base/ndarray/caxpby`][@stdlib/blas/ext/base/ndarray/caxpby] with `α = 1` and `β = 1` and performs element-wise addition between two complex vectors.

</section>

<!-- /.intro -->

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```javascript
var cxpy = require( '@stdlib/blas/ext/base/ndarray/cxpy' );
```

#### cxpy( arrays )

Adds elements of a one-dimensional single-precision complex floating-point ndarray to the corresponding elements of a second one-dimensional single-precision complex floating-point ndarray and assigns the results to the second ndarray.

```javascript
var Complex64Vector = require( '@stdlib/ndarray/vector/complex64' );

var x = new Complex64Vector( [ 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, -1.0, 0.0, 1.0 ] );
var y = new Complex64Vector( [ 2.0, 1.0, -1.0, 3.0, 4.0, 0.0 ] );

cxpy( [ x, y ] );
// y => <ndarray>[ <Complex64>[ 3.0, 3.0 ], <Complex64>[ 2.0, 2.0 ], <Complex64>[ 4.0, 1.0 ] ]
```

The function has the following parameters:

-   **arrays**: array-like object containing the following ndarrays:

    -   a one-dimensional input ndarray.
    -   a one-dimensional output ndarray.

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   The output ndarray is modified **in-place** (i.e., the output ndarray is **mutated**).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

<!-- eslint no-undef: "error" -->

```javascript
var discreteUniform = require( '@stdlib/random/array/discrete-uniform' );
var Complex64Vector = require( '@stdlib/ndarray/vector/complex64' );
var ndarray2array = require( '@stdlib/ndarray/to-array' );
var cxpy = require( '@stdlib/blas/ext/base/ndarray/cxpy' );

var opts = {
    'dtype': 'float32'
};

var x = new Complex64Vector( discreteUniform( 20, -100, 100, opts ) );
console.log( ndarray2array( x ) );

var y = new Complex64Vector( discreteUniform( 20, -100, 100, opts ) );
console.log( ndarray2array( y ) );

cxpy( [ x, y ] );
console.log( ndarray2array( y ) );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="c">

## C APIs

<section class="intro">

</section>

<!-- /.intro -->

<section class="usage">

### Usage

```c
#include "stdlib/blas/ext/base/ndarray/cxpy.h"
```

#### stdlib_blas_ext_cxpy( arrays )

Adds elements of a one-dimensional single-precision complex floating-point ndarray to the corresponding elements of a second one-dimensional single-precision complex floating-point ndarray and assigns the results to the second ndarray.

```c
void stdlib_blas_ext_cxpy( const struct ndarray *arrays[] );
```

The function accepts the following arguments:

-   **arrays**: `[in] struct ndarray**` list containing the following ndarrays:
    -   `[in] struct ndarray*` a one-dimensional input ndarray.
    -   `[inout] struct ndarray*` a one-dimensional output ndarray.

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

### Examples

```c
#include "stdlib/blas/ext/base/ndarray/cxpy.h"
#include "stdlib/ndarray/ctor.h"
#include "stdlib/complex/float32/ctor.h"
#include "stdlib/complex/float32/real.h"
#include "stdlib/complex/float32/imag.h"
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>

int main( void ) {
    // Create underlying byte arrays:
    float xbuf[] = { 1.0f, 2.0f, 3.0f, 4.0f, 5.0f, 6.0f, 7.0f, 8.0f };
    float ybuf[] = { 1.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f };

    // Define ndarray meta data:
    int8_t ndims = 1;
    int64_t shape[] = { 4 };
    int64_t stridesX[] = { 1 };
    int64_t stridesY[] = { 1 };
    int64_t offset = 0;

    // Create ndarray instances:
    struct ndarray *x = stdlib_ndarray_allocate( STDLIB_NDARRAY_COMPLEX64, xbuf, ndims, shape, stridesX, offset, STDLIB_NDARRAY_COLUMN_MAJOR );
    struct ndarray *y = stdlib_ndarray_allocate( STDLIB_NDARRAY_COMPLEX64, ybuf, ndims, shape, stridesY, offset, STDLIB_NDARRAY_COLUMN_MAJOR );

    // Set up the arrays argument:
    struct ndarray *arrays[] = { x, y };

    // Invoke the function:
    stdlib_blas_ext_cxpy( arrays );

    // Print the result:
    stdlib_complex64_t *ydata = (stdlib_complex64_t *)stdlib_ndarray_data( y );
    int64_t i;
    for ( i = 0; i < 4; i++ ) {
        printf( "y[ %li ] = %f + %fj\n", i, stdlib_complex64_real( ydata[ i ] ), stdlib_complex64_imag( ydata[ i ] ) );
    }

    // Free allocated memory:
    stdlib_ndarray_free( x );
    stdlib_ndarray_free( y );
}
```

</section>
